event_overview.title: About Yemen Conflict
event_overview.subject: Yemen Conflict
event_overview.summary: The Yemen conflict is a protracted political and armed struggle centered on the Houthi movement (Ansar Allah), Yemen’s internationally recognized government and other Yemeni armed and political actors. It intensified after the Houthis seized Sana’a in 2014 and became regionalized when a Saudi-led coalition intervened in 2015; United Nations-led efforts have sought a negotiated, Yemeni-led settlement.

facts.label: Origins and escalation
facts.value: The present phase escalated in mid-2014, when conflict between government forces, the Houthis and other armed groups intensified; Houthi forces and allied military units took Sana’a in September 2014.

facts.label: Regional intervention
facts.value: A coalition led by Saudi Arabia intervened militarily on 26 March 2015 at the request of then-President Abd Rabbuh Mansur Hadi, transforming the conflict into a regionalized war.

facts.label: Main conflict setting
facts.value: The conflict is principally within Yemen, but it has also involved cross-border hostilities and regional actors; the UN describes it as involving the Houthis, government forces and other armed groups, with consequences for the wider region.

facts.label: UN peace process
facts.value: The Office of the UN Special Envoy for Yemen was established in 2012 to support a Yemeni political transition and has continued to mediate toward a nationwide ceasefire and inclusive political process. A UN-brokered truce began on 2 April 2022, was extended twice, and expired on 2 October 2022.

facts.label: International legal and monitoring frame
facts.value: UN Security Council resolution 2452, adopted on 16 January 2019, established the UN Mission to Support the Hudaydah Agreement (UNMHA) to help implement the Stockholm Agreement’s arrangements for Hudaydah, Salif and Ras Issa ports, including ceasefire monitoring, redeployments and mine action.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers specific developments involving Houthi attacks affecting civilian aviation or critical infrastructure and related airport operations; it does not attempt to cover the full military, political, humanitarian or peace-process history of the Yemen conflict.
